_note: Answers use only facts published on brandywinefisheries.com plus general seafood knowledge. Nothing about the business is asserted that their own site does not state.

general.q: Where is the Brandywine Fisheries store?
general.a: 4731 Main St #1, Springfield, OR 97478 — open daily, 10am to 6pm. The phone is (541) 505-9686.

general.q: Which farmers markets does Brandywine attend?
general.a: Five market days across four cities: Eugene on Saturdays 9am–3pm and Tuesdays 10am–3pm at the Park Blocks at 8th & Oak, Corvallis on Saturdays 9am–1pm at 1st & Jackson, Bend on Wednesdays 11am–3pm in Brooks Alley downtown, and Portland on Saturdays 8:30am–2pm at the PSU market on SW Park and Montgomery.

No. Their site is explicit about it: the boat uses an "ICE" fish-hold that keeps the catch fresh from the point of catch to the time the boat docks. As they put it, not freezing the catch means they dock more often.

It is not a regulated term anywhere in the United States, so it always means whatever the seller's handling practice is. Brandywine ties the phrase to a specific practice — icing at the point of catch, docking often rather than freezing, and handling that avoids bruising the fish on board.

general.q: Where does the fish come from?
general.a: The Brandywine is an Oregon boat working out of Charleston harbor on the southern Oregon coast, where it was hand-built. Some items on the list — ahi, swordfish, mahi mahi, large raw shrimp and scallops — are not Oregon fisheries and are sourced rather than landed by the boat. Those are labelled as such throughout this site.

general.q: Can I order ahead for a farmers market?
general.a: Yes — there is a market pre-order list covering the fresh fish and most of the smoked line, including half-pound portions. It matters most at the short markets: Corvallis and Bend both run four hours, and popular cuts go early.

general.q: What is the most expensive fish you sell?
general.a: Halibut, at $38.95 a pound — more than chinook salmon at $29.95. The single most expensive item overall is the Smoked Seacuterie Board at $229.95.

general.q: What is the cheapest thing you sell?
general.a: Black mussels at $6.95. Bay shrimp are $9.00, mahi mahi $9.95, and Pacific rockfish $13.95 a pound — the least expensive fresh fillet.
At the Springfield store, yes — fresh oysters are one of the eight items listed as always carried there. They do not travel to the farmers market booths.

general.q: How long will fresh fish keep?
general.a: Two days for most fish, one to two for thin lean fillets like sole, two to three for fatty fish like black cod. Keep it on a rack over ice at the back of the bottom shelf, not sitting in melt water.

general.q: What should I cook if I don't really like fish?
general.a: Black cod. Its oil content makes it close to impossible to overcook and it tastes buttery rather than fishy. Most people who dislike fish have had it old or overcooked rather than actually disliking fish.

general.q: What temperature should I cook fish to?
general.a: The FDA guideline for finfish is 145°F. Most cooks pull well below it — salmon around 125°F, halibut 130–135°F, black cod 140°F, tuna seared with a 115°F center. Lean fish has almost no margin; fatty fish has plenty.

The albacore line is Brandywine's own — All Natural at $12, Alderwood Smoked at $15 and Jalapeño at $13, with case pricing up to $330. The tinned shelf also carries other producers' goods, including Ekone, Jose Gourmet, Matiz and Arroyabe, which are resold rather than made by Brandywine.

The Oregon commercial season is scheduled to open December 1 and usually opens later, once testing confirms the crab have filled with meat and biotoxin levels are safe. It traditionally runs into the following summer, closing in mid-August.

There is an online store on brandywinefisheries.com covering the canned, smoked and pantry lines. Fresh fish is handled through the store counter and the market pre-order list rather than shipped — check with them directly at (541) 505-9686 for anything specific.

general.q: Is the blue-green flesh in lingcod safe?
general.a: Yes. It is a natural pigment called biliverdin, it appears in roughly one lingcod in five, and it cooks out to pure white. It is not a defect and not a sign of anything wrong.
